problem: Learned navigation agents treat every episode as a fresh start with empty memory, ignoring images collected in earlier robot operations in the same environment. Existing ways to reuse such data (latent memory, topological maps, SLAM) need pose, depth or structured maps and do not extend easily to multi-robot data collection.
motivation: A realistic 'unboxing' deployment should let robots exploit earlier observations, and ideally share them across a fleet, without scene preparation. An unstructured image database queried with vision foundation models is simple, pose-free and scalable, and it can also supply goals for zero-shot task transfer.
key_idea: Augment an RL-trained ImageNav agent (DEBiT) with a pose-free retrieval database of first-person views, where DINOv2 or CLIP retrieves images and a frozen CroCo geometric FM plus a trainable context encoder turns them into directional cues for the policy; retrieval can also replace the goal for zero-shot tasks.
insight: The geometric FM is essential: replacing CroCo with a trained ResNet for context encoding drops SR from 83.0 to 79.1, back to baseline. Diversity (MMR) matters, and random context reduces performance to baseline levels (RANa-t static 77.0 SR, dynamic 80.3 SR), so the agent uses relevant context and filters misleading context. Oracle-context experiments show that structured path context (dynamic) has the most headroom: 98.3 SR and 87.9 SPL with oracle shortest path, versus 84.7 and 63.7 for the DINOv2-Graph.
method: Retrieval database D: unstructured first-person RGB views from earlier rollouts (about 1k per scene), with no pose or metadata; searched with DINOv2 features (CLIP/OpenCLIP for text goals) using nearest-neighbour search (Faiss)
Static context: top-N (N=8) DINOv2 neighbours of the goal, re-ranked with Maximum Marginal Relevance (beta=0.5, from a top-100 shortlist) for diversity; fixed per episode

Dynamic context (DINOv2-Graph): graph over database images with edges kept where DINOv2 cosine similarity exceeds 0.75, weights sqrt(1-s), Dijkstra shortest path between the nearest neighbours of the current observation and the goal; images sampled along the path form waypoint 'recommendations' recomputed each step

Context encoder c: the frozen CroCo binocular encoder of DEBiT embeds each context image against the observation and the goal; then either a Gumbel soft-max selector picks one embedding (works with any context size), or a 2-layer 4-head transformer with an MLP fuses all N tokens

Recurrent agent: half-width ResNet-18 observation encoder, CroCo goal comparison, action embedding and context feature go into a GRU (DEBiT GRU weights extended with padded input matrices and finetuned) and a linear actor-critic policy, trained with PPO for 200M steps with a geodesic-progress reward

Zero-shot task transfer: retrieve an image goal g^R from D (DINOv2 nearest neighbour for Instance-ImageNav; top-9 OpenCLIP images re-ranked by co-visibility for ObjectNav) so the ImageNav agent runs on new tasks without retraining
ObjectNav variant: OpenCLIP goal and observation features plus LOOK UP/DOWN actions, with context retrieved by softmax-normalised CLIP scores

setting.backbone: DEBiT (CroCo-based binocular encoder + half-width ResNet-18 + GRU policy) with a trained context encoder; DINOv2 and OpenCLIP frozen for retrieval
setting.model_size: RANa-t about 32-34M params, RANa-b about 66M+ (DEBiT-b 66M), RANa-L with adapters (larger)
setting.training_data: PPO in Habitat on Gibson (72 train scenes) for ImageNav, up to 200M steps; retrieval databases of about 1k-10k simulated images per scene; ObjectNav trained on HM3DSem (80 train scenes); zero-shot tasks use no extra training
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB 112x112 (plus retrieved database images); no depth or GPS/compass
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MOVE FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN LEFT/RIGHT 10°, STOP (plus LOOK UP/DOWN for ObjectNav)
setting.privileged: Access to a prior-exploration image database of the test scene (1k images, up to 50k-100k for zero-shot); ground-truth poses only in oracle/pose-graph ablations

numbers.extra: retrieval database of 1k images/scene at test; frozen encoders

results: RANa-b dynamic reaches 90.7 SR / 71.8 SPL on Gibson ImageNav versus 83.4 / 56.8 for DEBiT-b, and RANa-L with adapters reaches 94.5 / 76.2 versus 94.0 / 71.7. Zero-shot with a retrieved goal, it gets 58.7 SR on HM3D Instance-ImageNav, beating Mod-INN (56.1, which uses depth and odometry), and 36.6 SR on Gibson ObjectNav versus ZSON 31.3. RANa-t ObjectNav gets 52.1 SR versus 42.9 for the non-retrieval baseline and 42.4 for PSL, the best RGB-only baseline.
limitations: Assumes visual similarity is a proxy for spatial proximity, which fails in places; distracting context can make the agent circle instead of stopping
Zero-shot tasks need large retrieval databases (5k-50k images) and depend on retrieval accuracy; ObjectNav also needs a larger DB and a known category set for softmax
Evaluated only in simulation on a fairly clean, static database, with only a small sim-to-real test using goal images; the database is not updated online
